pr_title: Thread safe store support complicated index
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
In some scenarios, we expect to use complex joint indexing, not just through a single indexer.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
#109329

@roycaihw @liggitt 
I'm confused, my original intention was to provide the ability to join indexing, making it externally callable.

If I introduce a new Interface `JointIndexer`, I need to change some places where `Indexer` is used to use `JointIndexer`, such as `sharedIndexInformer`. I don't know if this is appropriate.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3beb8dc5967801bcaed4541b307dbcdbd86fda3d/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L302-L306

I noticed that there are no other classes in the internal code that implement the `Indexer` and `ThreadSafeStore` Interfaces. Can I just add methods to these two interfaces?

Can you help?

@roycaihw @liggitt @caesarxuchao @smarterclayton
I introduced a method to use my interface without any breaking changes, PTAL.
/retest

> In general, I want to see more concrete use cases of this feature before adding complexity to this package

`controller-runtime` need this func. Refer to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/blob/f46919744bee01060c9084a285e049afffd38c9d/pkg/cache/internal/cache_reader.go#L115-L138

There are too many operators using `controller-runtime`. We have some logic need to call List func with multi labelSelector but this can't use the index. When there are too many object to search, it will cost too much time.

Even we can convert labelSelector to fieldSelector but multi fieldSelector have not been supported now. To use index we can combine multiSelector to one but it's ugly and not friendly to users.

> The proposed "JointIndexer" interface only supports "AND" operation among indexers, is this the only combination of indexers we need to support? If not, we need to design a more general interface.

You are right, there is more than just `intersection` among indexers, I will try to design a more general interface.

Maybe we should support `symmetric difference`, `intersection`, `union` and `difference `.

> > In general, I want to see more concrete use cases of this feature before adding complexity to this package
> 
> `controller-runtime` need this func. Refer to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/blob/f46919744bee01060c9084a285e049afffd38c9d/pkg/cache/internal/cache_reader.go#L115-L138

> There are too many operators using `controller-runtime`. We have some logic need to call List func with multi labelSelector but this can't use the index. When there are too many object to search, it will cost too much time.

That's what I feel too.

> It seems that this can be achieved with either of:
> 
> - IndexKeys + ListKeys + Get: get the obj keys for cond1 and cond2, get all the obj keys, figure out obj keys that are in cond1 and in (all - cond2), convert the keys to objects
> - ByIndex + List: get the objects for cond1 and cond2, get all the objects, figure out objects that are in cond1 and in (all - cond2)
>
> Could you elaborate why we need this ByIndexes method?

As @roycaihw said, we had methods to do complicated index, but it seems not easy for users to do so. 
- Reason 1: we must care about `RWMutex` lock to ensure memory unchanged throughout the operation, I think it is easy to be ignored by user and should not be guaranteed by the user. 
- Reason 2: set operations between common index keys should be abstracted into common interfaces. It shouldn't make the caller complicated and error-prone.

> In general, I want to see more concrete use cases of this feature before adding complexity to this package

Hi @caesarxuchao, there are several general examples. I want to do complex `labelSelector`, `fieldSelector` to the `index cache`, or I want to combine multiple `indexers` to do index queries for custom operations. It is difficult to achieve these requirements with current capabilities. So I want to introduce new interface `JointIndexer`.

@caesarxuchao @liggitt @lavalamp @roycaihw @pohly Please consider it and sincerely hope for your suggestions. Do we really need this new feature?

I don't understand what keeps people from doing this today, or why it would be a good idea for us to do it for them. Can you please explain more.

> I don't understand what keeps people from doing this today, or why it would be a good idea for us to do it for them. Can you please explain more.

I think we need this feature for the following reasons:
1. Although users can use `IndexKeys` + `List` in combination,  the content of store may change during multiple indexing.
2. For convenience, when there is a scenario where multiple indexers are combined for joint indexing, we need to provide users with a more convenient interface. Different users should not be allowed to build the same wheel.

> Other than that, I think these scenarios are pretty common. For example I want to make complex field selector for pods cache like `status.phase!=Succeeded,spec.nodeName=node1`, unfortunately, it is difficult to achieve with current capabilities.
> 
> Once new feature comes, we can easily do it like:
> 
> ```go
> // multi index conditions with different operator
> indexConds := IndexConditions{
>         {Operator: selection.Equals, IndexName: nodeNameIndexer, IndexedValue: "node1"},
> 	{Operator: selection.NotEquals, IndexName: statusPhaseIndexer, IndexedValue: "Succeeded"},
> }
> 
> // JointIndexOptions applies to indexed result. General support pairwise
> // union, pairwise intersection and pairwise symmetric difference.
> // Meanwhile, custom index is also support.
> indexOpts := &JointIndexOptions{IndexType: UnionIndexType}
> 
> // do joint index by a convenient and safe way
> indexedPods := podStore.ByIndexes(indexConds, indexOpts)
> ```

I have similar scenarios where some of the same logic needs to be implemented over and over again in different projects.  If this capability can be provided it should reduce a lot of duplication of effort.

The main reason for this is that the content of the store will change during the user calls the index multiple times and then combines the index results. Users cannot avoid this because they cannot directly manipulate `ThreadSafeStore`.

I would first investigate the options which just let people perform multiple lists without releasing the lock.

Actually first I would try to be sure that this is actually a problem; if you do multiple lists from apiserver they don't happen at the same time either, does that really mean you can't do something useful?

Lock inside `threadSafeMap` seems to be private, I think users can not take the lock when they perform multiple lists. 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6e31c6531fbb83088d472e7a5680add214060967/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/thread_safe_store.go#L62-L71

Multiple lists from apiserver causes nothing bad. But `joint index form store` and `multi list form apiserver` are not same, `joint index form store` is like `a list request with multi conds fieldselector to apiserver`. In this scenario, the data in the list will no longer be changed when the filter is performed. So, should we make `joint index form store`  and `a list request with multi conds fieldselector to apiserver` behave in the same way?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6e31c6531fbb83088d472e7a5680add214060967/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L689-L709

If store changes are tolerable when performing multiple index combinations, then the only purpose of this issue is convenience :)

@FillZpp, @likakuli, Here,  I think our views are the same.
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/pull/1838#pullrequestreview-908261250
It is also possible to just list via one of the indexes, and then scan the result for the other conditions. I suspect for many indexes & queries, this would not be much slower.

In fact, as @likakuli said, "the list request cost O(n). When there are many object, it will cost too much time."

Sadly, it seems we have to admit that it gets slower and some of the same work will be repeated.

So, do we need to make a code change for all this? Please think about it. @lavalamp
I think I don't have time at the moment to give this as much thought as it needs. @deads2k or @liggitt are the other people who could approve an interface which supports this.
